subject: URGENT: Prefetch/locking causing lane starvation — Lumino AI impact
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@lumino.ai>

Date: 2029-09-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Latency/regression affecting production since 08:45 PT (Lumino)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a sharp spike in tail latency and 5xx errors starting ~08:45 PT this morning. Our dashboards show p99 from 320ms -> 2.4s and throughput falling by ~45%. The errors correlate with lots of 504/502 responses and a weird uptick in token rejections.

Attached is a small sample of logs and traces (lumino_error_snapshot.log, p99-traces-20290904.zip). Can you confirm whether this is on your side and what mitigation steps you can take immediately? This is affecting our customer-facing feature rollout.

We need an ETA for a fix or an intermediate mitigation (rate-limits, route change, or temporary model downscale).

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director of Integrations — Lumino AI

Thanks Priya — we're on it. Ben/Marissa: incoming customer-impact P1 from Lumino (LF-4721). Priority: restore p99 under 500ms and stop 5xx cascade.

Initial notes from the logs: lots of small prompt loads with bursty prefixes; traces show a growing queue on the priority lane and frequent KV eviction churn around the same time as the spike. Also seeing long batch assembly times for a subset of tenant requests (pile-ups at the batching layer).

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can you confirm whether per-tenant prefetch isolation and eviction thresholds for Lumino are intact?
- Marissa: ops to check if a rolling restart of the affected workers with a conservative KV eviction window is safe right now. We need an emergency mitigation and a communication plan to Lumino.

I've attached the customer logs for SRE review. Priya, we'll update you in 30 mins with what we try.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: p99-traces-20290904.zip (20MB - traces subset)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-04T09:37:00Z
Subject: RE: Latency/regression affecting production since 08:45 PT (Lumino)

Quick tech summary from initial triage:
1) Root pattern: tenant-prefetch interference + aggressive KV eviction + wide batch windows.
   - Lumino's request mix has many short-lived prefixes that trigger prefetches; prefetch queueing is occupying hot lanes.
   - Our current KV eviction policy (LRU with 60s TTL under memory pressure) is triggering repeatedly, causing cache churn and head-of-line (HOL) blocking when a hot key is evicted mid-inference.
   - Batching code has an upper assemble timeout (120ms) which in combination with queueing causes certain requests to join large batches, increasing latency variance.

2) Immediate mitigations we can try (low risk, can be done within 10–20 minutes):
   a) Flip Lumino traffic into the short-batch lane (config flag) to cap batch size and reduce assembly wait.
   b) Increase KV stable-window for Lumino's tenant to 5 minutes and raise eviction threshold to avoid oscillation.
   c) Disable cross-tenant prefetch for Lumino for the next 2 hours (isolates their hot prefixes).

3) Risk/impact:
   - a) will reduce throughput slightly for some hotspots but should drop p99 quickly.
   - b) increases memory usage; SRE needs to confirm capacity headroom.
   - c) removes prefetch benefits but prevents interference.

I'll implement (a)+(c) now as a canary for one hostpool and monitor traces. Marissa, can you confirm headroom for (b)? If safe, we'll apply (b) cluster-wide for Lumino hosts.

I'll post a short play-by-play to the incident channel.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops_rollback_plan.pdf (2 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-04T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Latency/regression affecting production since 08:45 PT (Lumino)

Acted on Ben's plan — applied short-batch lane and disabled cross-tenant prefetch for Lumino on a single hostpool (us-west-2-a) at 09:55 PT. Observed effects: p99 dropped from ~2.4s to ~540ms within ~3 minutes, errors dropped by ~78%.

SRE notes:
- We have ~18% memory headroom across the Lumino-affinity pool; applying the extended KV stable-window (5m) cluster-wide is likely safe but will increase memory pressure during other tenant peaks. Recommend doing that after we get agreement from capacity.
- Rolling restart not required yet; we're holding until (b) is scheduled.

Customer comms: Vanessa, I suggest we offer Lumino two items — (1) a short incident credit for the degraded window, (2) a follow-up architecture session to tune their prefetch/usage patterns with recommended client-side backoff.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Latency/regression affecting production since 08:45 PT (Lumino) — exec summary

Thanks all for the quick response and solid remediation. Summary for exec sync / Lumino exec:

- What happened: Prefetch isolation failure + aggressive KV eviction resulted in repeated hot-key evictions; that in turn caused head-of-line blocking inside the batching path and produced p99 spikes and 5xx cascades for Lumino.
- Immediate outcome: short-batch lane + disabled cross-tenant prefetch on a canary hostpool restored p99 to ~400–550ms and reduced error rate by ~80% within 5 minutes.
- Next action (24–72h):
   1) Apply raised KV stable-window (5m) for Lumino across their affinity hosts after verifying memory headroom (Marissa).
   2) Ship a small runtime change to add tenant-prefetch throttles and soft isolation (Ben + Eng) — target patch ETA 48h.
   3) Follow-up: automated detection rule for eviction-churn signatures to auto-isolate affected tenants.
- Customer remediation: offer a pro-rated credit for the incident window and schedule a technical review with Lumino to adjust client-side prefix patterns. Vanessa: please coordinate the credit amount with Finance/CS.

I approve proceeding with (1) after SRE confirms headroom. If memory constraints block (1), escalate to me and we will provision temporary capacity for Lumino to avoid repeat regressions.

Also: let's capture this incident as a Priority-Learnings doc and assign owners for the follow-ups. Assignments: Ben -> prefetch throttle patch, Marissa -> KV-window rollout and monitoring, Vanessa -> customer comms/credit, Grace -> incident doc.

Jonas Weber
VP Engineering — Redwood Inference
